newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nisseki House aims at 1998/99 profit.
newsitem.headline: Nisseki House aims at 1998/99 profit.

text.p: Nisseki House Industry Co Ltd said on Friday it is aiming to post a profit in its next business year ending March 1999.

In its latest three-year plan, Nisseki House, which makes prefabricated houses, targeted a parent current profit of 300 million yen in 1998/99 on sales of 53 billion yen, followed by a current profit of 1.60 billion yen on sales of 61 billion yen in 1999/2000.

The company earlier revised its forecast for 1996/97 to a parent current loss of 14.50 billion yen, above an earlier projected loss of 9.10 billion yen. The company posted a profit of 760 million yen in 1995/96.
In the three-year plan, the company intends to boost its sales by developing a new model of apartment house and by developing and marketing new low-priced single-family houses in 1997/98.
The company said it plans to improve its productivity and reduce production costs by using interchangeable components for housing frames.

In January this year, Nisseki House ousted its president Saburo Horinouchi, who had been missing with unknown reason since December 11, and appointed his eldest son, Yuji, as vice president and acting president.
